drafted_from: tool:trade-an-instagram-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token's row in tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json (job, description, input_schema, invoke) and the folder's test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs, whose stand-in answers give the reply and the held word
start_here: Say to your AI: "Trade an Instagram sign-in code for its short token for the new connection service_connection:instagram:2a6f0c93 with the code made-up-code-4f9a2c." It runs tool:trade-an-instagram-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token and tells you the tokens are kept in the vault without showing any of them.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it sends one request to Instagram for the connection it is handed and keeps the tokens in the vault as that connection's fields.
instructions: 1. Do not run this by hand: tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service runs it for you at the sign-in callback, after you open the sign-in address it gave you. Start that tool first (its kit shows the call) and keep the connection_id it answers: service_connection:instagram:2a6f0c93 is the shape.

2. To run this step alone, the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:trade-an-instagram-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token and the input the worked example shows (the connection by its handle only, the code the service handed back, the callback address the sign-in was started with).
3. Read what comes back: the service's reply with every kept token already replaced by the word [held]. The short-lived token now sits in the vault as the connection's short_lived_access_token field.
4. A refusal (a used-up code, a wrong callback address) is shown as the service's own error; nothing is kept, so start the sign-in again for a new link.

worked_examples.title: Trade an Instagram sign-in code for its short token for a made-up connection
worked_examples.ask: Trade an Instagram sign-in code for its short token for service_connection:instagram:2a6f0c93.
worked_examples.given: From tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs (its stand-in for this tool's answer, made up the way the engine answers: every token is already the held word "[held]", because reply_holds_values keeps each token in the vault before the reply is read): the code and callback address go to api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token (no PKCE verifier).. Input: {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:instagram:2a6f0c93"},"code":"made-up-code-4f9a2c","redirect_uri":"https://app.gettrillion.ai/work/api/connect/callback"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"access_token":"[held]","user_id":17800000000000000}. The short-lived token now sits in the vault as the connection's short_lived_access_token field.
